cases.name: AnyCheck
cases.headline: Document review with Orbit in context.
cases.summary: Document extraction and review, Orbit AI chat and configurable processing workflows at Fintelite Group.
cases.coverAlt: AnyCheck project cover combining native document extraction, Orbit AI chat and the Orbit mascot
cases.intro: A document feature is only one part of a business application. People also need to choose a service, configure what it extracts, review the output and connect the result to the next step.

sections.title: The product
paragraphs: AnyCheck brings document verification and extraction into a shared workspace. Its capabilities include custom extraction templates, bank statement analysis, an AI assistant and a visual Workflow Builder.
The workflow tooling lets users configure a process from the node types available to their organisation. Upload and results views connect that process to the documents being handled.

sections.title: My contribution
paragraphs: At Fintelite, I lead technical direction and help connect architecture and engineering delivery with Product and Data team priorities.

My document-AI experience includes OCR pipelines, LLM integration and work with the Data Team on extraction improvements. I work alongside the engineers and product teams responsible for the wider platform.

sections.title: From document to next action
items: Review a document beside its structured fields and line items.
Ask Orbit about the document without leaving its context.
Connect extraction and follow-up steps in the visual Workflow Builder.
Monitor the organisation’s activity, credits and review queue.
Configure custom extraction fields and refine their definitions.
Inspect financial-document account totals and transaction-level records.

sections.title: For a similar project
paragraphs: This work is relevant to a team building document-heavy business software: the application around an AI capability, the review interfaces and the processes that make the output useful.
The related engineering experience spans application architecture, technical delivery and collaboration across Fintelite’s products.

cases.name: Jagoan Voucher
cases.headline: A marketplace, with a creator side.
cases.summary: Voucher purchasing, order flows and realtime creator tools in one web product.
cases.coverAlt: Jagoan Voucher marketplace and native creator donation-alert preview, composed on a dark project cover
cases.intro: Jagoan Voucher combines two product flows: buying game vouchers and supporting creators. Each needs a clear interface, while orders, balances and realtime updates depend on the backend behind it.

sections.title: The product
paragraphs: The marketplace covers product selection, checkout and order status. Creator-facing tools include donation views, a dashboard and an Overlay Studio for configuring OBS browser-source widgets.
The overlay tooling includes alert and goal interfaces, with additional widgets for creator use. A demo state is separate from a live donation or payment.

sections.title: My contribution
paragraphs: I worked on the frontend and backend. The scope spans the web interfaces and the application services supporting the marketplace and creator tools.
For the portfolio, the useful example is the connection between a product page, its order flow and the tools a creator uses after signing in.

Denomination selection, checkout and order tracking.
Creator dashboard and donation views.
Overlay Studio and OBS alert configuration.
Realtime interfaces supported by backend services.

The frontend and backend need to agree on order states, balances and user roles. The marketplace and creator interfaces show different parts of that shared product.

cases.name: GoMUSI
cases.headline: A request, through its next steps.
cases.summary: Public-service information, multi-step applications and tools for managing forms and service flows.
cases.coverAlt: Reference-based GoMUSI cover with original service-flow and applicant-form views presented in realistic phone hardware
cases.intro: A service application has two sides: the person submitting information and the people reviewing it. GoMUSI connects service information, forms and the steps a request moves through.

sections.title: The product
paragraphs: GoMUSI organises public-service information and applications around forms and a sequence of service steps. Its interfaces include service selection, submissions, review and submission details.
Administrative tools support the management of services, forms and ordered flow or wizard steps.

sections.title: My contribution
paragraphs: I worked on the frontend and backend. The scope includes applicant-facing interfaces and the application services behind forms and service flows.
The administrative side is part of the product scope: teams need to manage what applicants see and the stages a service requires, rather than relying only on a fixed public form.

sections.title: Selected product flows
items: A catalogue of services and their requirements.
Multi-step application and information collection.
Submission details, progress and review.
Administrative form, service and flow management.

sections.title: For a similar project
paragraphs: This work is relevant to a business or institution replacing disconnected forms with a structured application process.
That experience also applies to application portals, intake workflows and administrative tools that need to work together.

cases.name: MyTimor
cases.headline: Three apps, one connected service.
cases.summary: Customer, driver and merchant applications for transport, goods delivery and food ordering in Timor-Leste.
cases.coverAlt: Reference-based MyTimor cover showing delivery booking, restaurant menu and completed delivery in integrated phone frames
cases.intro: Customers, drivers and merchants take part in the same service, but each needs a different mobile workflow. MyTimor brings those roles together for transport, delivery and food ordering.

sections.title: The product
paragraphs: MyTimor supports transport, goods delivery and food ordering in Timor-Leste. Its customer, driver and merchant applications serve different parts of an order, with T-PAY included in the product's payment flow.

sections.title: My contribution
paragraphs: I developed the customer, driver and merchant applications in Flutter. I also worked on the database schema, REST APIs and real-time communication connecting the mobile applications.
I handled Android Play Store publication and internal testing channels.

sections.title: Scope of the work
items: Role-specific customer, driver and merchant applications.
Backend interfaces and a shared data model for mobile workflows.
Real-time communication between parts of the service.
Android distribution and internal testing.

sections.title: For a similar project
paragraphs: This project is relevant to a business planning a marketplace or delivery service that needs more than one mobile interface and the APIs connecting them.
The interfaces show connected but distinct responsibilities: customers choose and place orders, drivers verify deliveries, and merchants maintain menus and operating hours.

cases.name: E-Library UNTL
cases.headline: A digital library, beyond its catalogue.
cases.summary: A reader-facing website, web administrator interface and backend REST API for an online university library.
cases.coverAlt: E-Library UNTL presentation showing the reader-facing website and book catalogue
cases.intro: Readers need to find a book and understand what it contains. A digital library also needs the interfaces and services behind that catalogue.

sections.title: The product
paragraphs: E-Library UNTL is an online library for Universidade Nacional Timor Lorosa'e. The reader-facing website presents book discovery, subject categories and individual book pages.
The wider product also includes an E Biblioteca UNTL mobile reader with subject departments and in-app reading.

sections.title: My contribution
paragraphs: I developed the website frontend, the web administrator interface and the REST API for the backend.
The work covered the public catalogue as well as the interfaces and services used to manage it. The gallery below shows the reader-facing side.

cases.name: Sribuu
cases.headline: Everyday finance, built for mobile.
cases.summary: A personal-finance product for iOS and Android, with Flutter development, clean architecture and mobile-team leadership.
cases.coverAlt: Sribuu mobile product presentation with its original turquoise identity
cases.intro: I built the iOS and Android applications with Flutter, then led the mobile team. My work covered implementation, application architecture, code review and improvements to the apps.

sections.title: The product
paragraphs: Sribuu is a personal-finance application. Its public product guides describe recording transactions, planning category-based monthly budgets and tracking financial goals.
These product capabilities explain the context of the work. They do not establish that every feature or current interface was part of the version I worked on.

sections.title: My contribution
paragraphs: From June to December 2021, I developed the iOS and Android applications with Flutter and clean architecture.
From January 2022 to December 2023, I worked as Senior Frontend Engineer / Mobile Team Lead: leading the mobile team, researching improvements, reviewing code and optimising the applications.

sections.title: Engineering beyond one screen
items: Flutter implementation across iOS and Android.
Clean architecture and application structure.
Code review, technical research and mobile-team leadership.
